text.heading: Ether 12:10–12
text.content: Behold it was by faith that they of old were called after the holy order of God. [c]1631302601[/c] [c]1631304701[/c] [c]1631304101[/c] Wherefore, by faith was the law of Moses given. [c]1631418101[/c] [c]1631402601[/c] [c]1631404701[/c] But in the gift of his Son hath God prepared a more excellent way; [c]1631416601[/c] [c]1631405401[/c] [c]1631404101[/c] and it is by faith that it hath been fulfilled. For if there be no faith among the children of men God can do no miracle among them; [c]1631518101[/c] [c]1631304801[/c] [c]1631308201[/c] [c]1631507201[/c] [c]1631504701[/c] [c]1631505401[/c] [c]1631502601[/c] [c]1631504101[/c] [c]1631506601[/c] wherefore, he showed not himself until after their faith. [c]1631311101[/c]

notes.title: “By faith…called after the holy order”
notes.text: See Alma 13.3.

Because the law of Moses was fulfilled in Christ, the gospel as taught among the Nephites appears to be the more excellent way that Moroni has in mind, but see 1 Cor 12.31, where it refers to charity.
See 3 Ne 19.35;Morm 9.20n.

narration.description: Faith is what caused {Alma|alma2} and {Amulek|amulek}’s prison to fall, faith is what cause the change in the {Lamanites|lamanites} that {Nephi|nephi2} and {Lehi|lehi4} taught, and faith is what empowered the {sons of Mosiah|sons-of-mosiah} on their missions.

text.heading: Ether 12:13–16
text.content: Behold, it was the faith of Alma and Amulek that caused the prison to tumble to the earth. [c]1631604701[/c] [c]1631602601[/c] Behold, it was the faith of Nephi and Lehi that wrought the change upon the Lamanites, [c]1631716601[/c] [c]1631704101[/c] [c]1631704701[/c] that they were baptized with fire and with the Holy Ghost. Behold, it was the faith of Ammon and his brethren which wrought so great a miracle among the Lamanites. [c]1631802601[/c] [c]1631907201[/c] Yea, and even all they who wrought miracles wrought them by faith, [c]1631816601[/c] [c]1631904701[/c] [c]1631101201[/c] even those who were before Christ and also those who were after. [c]1631611101[/c]

people.name: Alma2
people.title: Son of Alma1, first chief judge, high priest

people.name: Ammon2
people.title: Son of Mosiah2, missionary to Lamanites

people.name: Lamanites
people.title: Descendant of Laman1, later any person who rejects the gospel

notes.text: See Alma 14.26–29.

notes.title: “that they were baptized with fire and with the Holy Ghost”
notes.text: Hel 5
See Hel 5.35–49n. According to Hel 5.41, 47, as well as 3 Ne 9.20, it was the faith of the Lamanites themselves, rather than that of Nephi2 and Lehi4, that resulted in their baptism with fire.

notes.title: “the faith of Ammon and his brethren which wrought so great a miracle among the Lamanites”
notes.text: Alma 17–26
See Alma 17–26.

narration.description: Similarly, The {three disciples|three-nephite-disciples} of {Christ|jesus-christ} were granted their wish only after they exercised faith.

text.heading: Ether 12:17–18
text.content: And it was by faith that the three disciples obtained a promise that they should not taste of death; [c]1631804101[/c] [c]1632002601[/c] and they obtained not the promise until after their faith. [c]1632104701[/c] And neither at any time hath any wrought miracles until after their faith; [c]1631604801[/c] [c]1632104101[/c] wherefore they first believed in the Son of God. [c]1632107201[/c] [c]1632011101[/c] [c]1631005401[/c]

notes.title: “Miracles Come After The Trial of Faith”
notes.text: Verse 18 restates the theme of verse 6, that miracles come after the trial of faith.

narration.description: The faith of some was so strong, that they could not be kept from within the veil; the {brother of Jared|jareds-brother} was one such, and he saw the finger of the {Lord|jesus-christ}.

text.heading: Ether 12:19–21
text.content:
And there were many whose faith was so exceedingly strong, even before Christ came, who could not be kept from within the veil, [c]1632204101[/c] [c]1632206601[/c] [c]1632412101[/c] but truly saw with their eyes the things which they had beheld with an eye of faith, [c]1631608201[/c] and they were glad.

And behold, we have seen in this record that one of these was the brother of Jared; for so great was his faith in God, that when God put forth his finger he could not hide it from the sight of the brother of Jared, [c]1632204801[/c] [c]1632204701[/c] because of his word which he had spoken unto him, [c]1632316601[/c] which word he had obtained by faith. [c]1632211101[/c]

And after the brother of Jared had beheld the finger of the Lord, because of the promise which the brother of Jared had obtained by faith, the Lord could not withhold anything from his sight; [c]1632218101[/c] [c]1632407201[/c] wherefore he showed him all things, for he could no longer be kept without the veil. [c]1632416601[/c]

notes.title: “God Finger Could Not Hide It from the Sight of the Brother of Jared”
notes.text: After Nephite examples, Moroni cites the Jaredite example of the brother of Jared’s powerful faith.
See Ether 3.6–28.

narration.description: Promises from {God|god} to the {Gentiles|gentiles} are also to be received by faith.

text.heading: Ether 12:22
text.content: And it is by faith that my fathers have obtained the promise that these things should come unto their brethren through the Gentiles; [c]1632502601[/c] [c]1632504101[/c] [c]1632507201[/c] therefore the Lord hath commanded me, yea, even Jesus Christ. [c]1632504701[/c]

people.name: God
people.title: A reference to diety, be it Yahweh (יהוה); Jesus, or God the Father.

notes.title: “These Things”
notes.text: The Book of Mormon, and especially the Plates of Ether.

notes.title: “The Lord hath commanded me”
notes.text: That is, to write this record.

narration.description: {Moroni|moroni2} laments to the {Lord|jesus-christ}, telling him that people will mock his writings, because of his weaknesses; he is deeply concerned about the effectiveness of his message in light of the limitations of written records.

text.heading: Ether 12:23–25
text.content:
And I said unto him:

“Lord, the Gentiles will mock at these things, [c]1632606601[/c] [c]1632612101[/c] because of our weakness in writing; [c]1632604701[/c] [c]1632604101[/c] [c]1632602601[/c] for Lord thou hast made us mighty in word by faith, [c]1632616601[/c] but thou hast not made us mighty in writing; [c]1632608201[/c] [c]1632704101[/c] [c]1632704701[/c] for thou hast made all this people that they could speak much, because of the Holy Ghost which thou hast given them; [c]1632618101[/c] [c]1632804101[/c]

And thou hast made us that we could write but little, because of the awkwardness of our hands. Behold, thou hast not made us mighty in writing like unto the brother of Jared, for thou madest him that the things which he wrote were mighty even as thou art, unto the overpowering of man to read them. Thou hast also made our words powerful and great, even that we cannot write them; wherefore, when we write we behold our weakness, [c]1632804701[/c] and stumble because of the placing of our words; and I fear lest the Gentiles shall mock at our words. [c]1632617101[/c]” [c]1632411101[/c]

people.name: Moroni2
people.title: Son of Mormon2, last of Nephites

notes.text: Other discussions of weakness in writing occur at 2 Ne 3.18–21; 33.1–4, 11; like Nephi before him, Moroni is also laying claim to the prophecy of Joseph of Egypt in 2 Ne 3.

notes.title: “The things which he wrote”
notes.text: Moroni is referring to the sealed account of the brother of Jared’s vision; see Ether 3.21–28.

narration.description: The {Lord|jesus-christ} reassures {Moroni|moroni2} that those who mock will mourn, and that the {Lord|jesus-christ} gives weaknesses to people so that they humble themselves; the {Lord|jesus-christ} will prove that faith, hope and charity leads to him: the fountain of all righteousness.

text.heading: Ether 12:26–28
text.content:
And when I had said this, the Lord spake unto me, saying:

“Fools mock, [c]1632605401[/c] but they shall mourn; [c]1632904701[/c] [c]1632913101[/c] [c]1632904101[/c] [c]1632912101[/c] and my grace is sufficient for the meek, [c]1633007203[/c] [c]1632912102[/c] that they shall take no advantage of your weakness; [c]1633004101[/c] And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. [c]1633018102[/c] [c]1633012101[/c]

I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; [c]1632904801[/c] [a]36[/a] [c]1632903101[/c] [c]1633012102[/c] [c]1633005401[/c] [c]1633008201[/c] [c]1632909101[/c] and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; [c]1633018101[/c] [c]1633005403[/c] [c]1633007202[/c] [c]1633012103[/c] [c]1633001201[/c] for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them. [c]1633104101[/c] [c]1633002601[/c] [c]1633012104[/c] [c]1633005402[/c] [c]1633007201[/c] [c]1632915101[/c] [c]1633004701[/c]

Behold, I will show unto the Gentiles their weakness and I will show unto them that faith, hope and charity bringeth unto me—the fountain of all righteousness.” [c]1632504801[/c] [c]1633116601[/c] [c]1632911101[/c] [c]1633104701[/c] [c]1633105401[/c] [c]1633102601[/c]

people.name: Moroni2
people.title: Son of Mormon2, last of Nephites

notes.text: God does not deny that Moroni’s writings are weak, but he asserts that weak things—including the BoM itself—can become strong to those who receive them in faith. Indeed, weaknesses are gifts that can lead to humility and grace.

notes.title: “My grace is sufficient…weak things become strong”

notes.text: This verse introduces what follows, as the argument moves from faith (Ether 12:29–31) to hope (Ether 12:32) to love, or charity (Ether 12:33–35).

notes.title: “Fountain of all righteousness”
notes.text: See Ether 8.26n.

narration.description: {Moroni|moroni2} is comforted, and rejoices in the power of faith and his hope for a place in {God|god}’s kingdom.

text.heading: Ether 12:29–35
text.content:
And I, Moroni, having heard these words, was comforted, and said:

“O Lord, thy righteous will be done, [c]1633216601[/c] for I know that thou workest unto the children of men according to their faith; [c]1633208201[/c] [c]1633313102[/c] [c]1633202601[/c] For the brother of Jared said unto the mountain Zerin, Remove—and it was removed. [c]1633104801[/c] [c]1633304801[/c] [c]1633303101[/c] [c]1633313101[/c] [c]1633312101[/c] [c]1633302601[/c] And if he had not had faith it would not have moved; [c]1633204701[/c] [c]1633304101[/c] wherefore thou workest after men have faith. [c]1633407201[/c] [c]1633304701[/c] [c]1633206601[/c]

For thus didst thou manifest thyself unto thy disciples; [c]1633504801[/c] [c]1633416601[/c] [c]1633402601[/c] for after they had faith, [c]1633305401[/c] and did speak in thy name, thou didst show thyself unto them in great power. [c]1633416602[/c]

And I also remember that thou hast said that thou hast prepared a house for man, [c]1633416603[/c] [c]1633404701[/c] [c]1633504101[/c] yea, even among the mansions of thy Father, in which man might have [c]1633516601[/c] a more excellent hope; [c]1633505401[/c] [c]1633504701[/c] [c]1633512101[/c] wherefore man must hope, [c]1633502601[/c] or he cannot receive an inheritance in the place which thou hast prepared. [c]1633211101[/c] [c]1633514201[/c]

And again, I remember that thou hast said that thou hast loved the world, even unto the laying down of thy life for the world, [c]1633707201[/c] [c]1633604701[/c] [c]1633604101[/c] that thou mightest take it again to prepare a place for the children of men.

And now I know that this love which thou hast had for the children of men is charity; [c]1633605401[/c] [c]1633608201[/c] [c]1633601201[/c] [c]1633602601[/c] [c]1633704701[/c] [c]1633704101[/c] wherefore, except men shall have charity they cannot inherit that place which thou hast prepared in the mansions of thy Father. [c]1633712101[/c] [c]1633804701[/c]

Wherefore, I know by this thing which thou hast said, that if the Gentiles have not charity, [c]1633404101[/c] because of our weakness, that thou wilt prove them, [c]1633204101[/c] and take away their talent, yea, even that which they have received, and give unto them who shall have more abundantly.” [c]1633611101[/c]

text.heading: Ether 12:36
text.content: And it came to pass that I prayed unto the Lord that he would give unto the Gentiles grace, [c]1633904701[/c] that they might have charity. [c]1633904101[/c] [c]1633913101[/c] [c]1633906601[/c]

text.content: And now I, Moroni, bid farewell unto the Gentiles, [c]1634104701[/c] [c]1634102601[/c] yea, and also unto my brethren whom I love, [c]1634104101[/c] until we shall meet before the judgment–seat of Christ, [c]1634005401[/c] where all men shall know that my garments are not spotted with your blood. [c]1634113101[/c] [c]1634204701[/c] [c]1634112101[/c] [c]1634105401[/c] And then shall ye know that I have seen Jesus, [c]1634218101[/c] [c]1634103101[/c] [c]1634105402[/c] and that he hath talked with me face to face, [c]1634208201[/c] [c]1634213101[/c] and that he told me in plain humility, even as a man telleth another in mine own language, [c]1634204101[/c] concerning these things; [c]1634304701[/c] And only a few have I written, [c]1634304101[/c] because of my weakness in writing. notes.text: Moroni<sup>2</sup> closes his final comment section with phrasing similar to that used by Mormon<sup>2</sup> as he ended his letter at Moro 9.26, a text Moroni<sup>2</sup> would have had in his possession but has not yet included in his record.
That is, “I would recommend that you seek” [archaic usage]

That is, in the Old and New Testaments. Because the word apostle is consistently used to refer to Jesus’s apostles in the Old World (as opposed to the Nephite twelve disciples), this is one of only two specific references in the Book of Mormon to the New Testament as a whole; the other is at 1 Ne 13.39.

notes.title: “I would commend you to seek”
notes.text: I would recommend that you seek.

notes.title: “Of whom the prophets and apostles have written”
notes.text: That is, in the Old and New Testaments. Because the word apostle is consistently used to refer to Jesus’s apostles in the Old World (as opposed to the Nephite twelve disciples), this is one of only two specific references in the BoM to the NT as a whole; the other is at 1 Ne 13.39. Of course, prophets could also include God’s messengers to the Nephites.

notes.title: “The grace of God the Father…Lord Jesus Christ…be and abide in you forever”
notes.text: Moroni closes his final comment section with phrasing similar to that used by Mormon as he ended his letter at Moro 9.26—a text Moroni would have had in his possession but has not yet included in his record. He may have felt that his “weakness in writing” could be remedied by borrowing the more eloquent words of others.

text.heading: Ether 13:1–3
text.content:
And now I, Moroni, proceed to finish my record concerning the destruction of the people of whom I have been writing. [c]1634504801[/c] [c]1634511101[/c] [c]1634504701[/c] [c]1634504101[/c]

For behold, they rejected all the words of Ether; [c]1634517102[/c] [c]1634608201[/c] for he truly told them of all things, from the beginning of man; [c]1634605401[/c] [c]1634602601[/c] and that after the waters had receded from off the face of this land it became a choice land above all other lands, [c]1634616601[/c] a chosen land of the Lord; [c]1634618101[/c] [c]1634604101[/c] [c]1634604701[/c] wherefore the Lord would have [c]1634616602[/c] that all men should serve him who dwell upon the face thereof. [c]1634611101[/c] [c]1634612101[/c]

And that it was the place of the New Jerusalem, [c]1634604801[/c] [c]1634705402[/c] [c]1634609101[/c] [c]1634506601[/c] [c]1634613101[/c] [c]1634708201[/c] [c]1634501101[/c] [c]1634501201[/c] which should come down out of heaven, [c]1634717101[/c] [c]1634616603[/c] [c]1634705401[/c] [c]1634704701[/c] [c]1634704101[/c] [c]1634713101[/c] [c]1634712101[/c] and the holy sanctuary of the Lord.

notes.text: It is unexpected that Ether would write of the New Jerusalem since the Jaredites had left the Old World many centuries before David established the old Jerusalem as a capital city. Similarly, the references to Joseph and Abraham would seem extraneous to Ether’s audience since the Jaredites were not of the house of Israel, nor were they descendants of Abraham. Perhaps Moroni is expanding on Ether’s original prophecies, as he did at Ether 12.6–41.

notes.title: “After the waters had receded”
notes.text: See Gen 8.13–14. Moroni had written earlier at Ether 2.8–12 of the necessity for those living in this land to serve God.

notes.title: “The New Jerusalem, which shall come down out of heaven”
notes.text: Rev 3.12; 21.2, both of which refer to the heavenly counterpart and eventual replacement for the historic city (the new city is described in detail at Rev 21.9–22.5). The BoM, by contrast, envisions the New Jerusalem as an earthly counterpart on the American continent built by latter-day Lehites with assistance from the Gentiles. The only other BoM references to the New Jerusalem, outside of Ether 13, are 3 Ne 20.22; 21.23–25.
<i>Holy sanctuary” seems to refer to a temple complex within the New Jerusalem.

narration.description: {Ether|ether} saw the days of {Christ|jesus-christ}, the rebuilding of the [Old Jerusalem|jerusalem-1], and the establishment of the [New Jerusalem|zion].

text.heading: Ether 13:4–6
text.content:
Behold, Ether saw the days of Christ, [c]1634816601[/c] [c]1634808201[/c] and he spake concerning a New Jerusalem upon this land. [i]3503[/i] [c]1634603101[/c] [c]1634913101[/c]

And he spake also concerning the house of Israel, [c]1635004701[/c] and the Jerusalem from whence Lehi should come—after it should be destroyed it should be built up again, [c]1635008201[/c] [c]1634912101[/c] a holy city unto the Lord; [c]1634904801[/c] [c]1634916601[/c] wherefore, it could not be a new Jerusalem for it had been in [c]1634916602[/c] a time of old; [c]1634904101[/c] but it should be built up again, and become a holy city of the Lord; [c]1634805401[/c] [c]1634908201[/c] and it should be built unto the house of Israel.

And that a New Jerusalem should be built upon this land, [c]1634718101[/c] [c]1634904701[/c] unto the remnant of the seed of Joseph, [c]1634916603[/c] [c]1635006601[/c] for which things there has been a type. [c]1634717101[/c] [c]1634711101[/c]

notes.text: This was the most-cited passage from the BoM in early LDS literature (1830–46), closely followed by 3 Ne 21.1–7 (on the BoM and the gathering of Israel) and 2 Ne 30.3–6 (on the BoM and the restoration of Native Americans).

notes.title: “and it should be built unto”
notes.text: 𝒫 built up unto

Moroni perceives a type, or a parallel, between Joseph’s taking refuge in Egypt and some of his descendants taking refuge in the New World. The similarities are that both Joseph and the Lehites survive abroad, unknown to their kinsmen back home, and perform a work there that will save their relatives (a father in one case and posterity in the other). In addition, neither will return to their native land.

narration.description: The {Lord|jesus-christ} is merciful to the remnant of {Joseph|joseph1}’s seed.

notes.title: “and from the north countries”
notes.text: That is, the lost tribes; see Jer 15.16; 31.8
Here the people themselves, and not just their clothing, have been cleansed by the blood of the Lamb; this is also the case at 1 Ne 12.11; Morm 9.6; Moro 10.33.

notes.title: “Gathered in…from the north countries”
notes.text: Referring to the lost tribes; see Jer 23.7–8; 31.8.

This antimetabole, or chiastic aphorism, is attached to three different stories in the NT: Mt 19.30 (Mk 10.31); Mt 20.16; Lk 13.30. At 1 Ne 13.42 and Jacob 5.63, the saying is applied to the Jews and the Gentiles. Here it is unclear whether the first and last refer to the two Jerusalems, or to the two branches of Israel located in the Western and Eastern Hemispheres.

notes.title: “And I was about to write more, but I am forbidden”
notes.text: For additional instances of the Lord exercising editorial control over the contents of the Book of Mormon, see 1 Ne 14.28; 3 Ne 26.11–12; 28.25.

notes.title: “But I am forbidden”
notes.text: For additional instances of the Lord exercising editorial control over the contents of the BoM, see 1 Ne 14.28;3 Ne 26.11–12;28.25.

notes.title: “Great and marvelous were the prophecies of Ether”

notes.title: “Esteemed him as naught”
notes.text: Regarded him as worthless.

“Cavity of a rock” occurs four times in this chapter and also at 1 Ne 3.27, perhaps referring not to a cave but rather a crevice in the rocks, as at Isa 2.19; 7.19; Jer 16.16 (KJV: “holes of the rocks”).

notes.title: “A few more things”
notes.text: The chapters that follow include instructions for worship and ritual, particularly in areas where the Bible is not clear. They may have been provided as a service to latter-day Gentiles, but Moroni primarily has in mind the descendants of the Lamanites.

notes.title: “I write…unto my brethren, the Lamanites”
notes.text: The book of Moroni is framed by an inclusio that begins here and concludes at Moroni 10.1. There is deep pathos in Moroni’s writing for the descendants of the people who have slain his family and friends, and who may kill him as well (Morm 8.2–5).

notes.title: “as he laid his hands upon them”
notes.text: These words were promised at 3 Ne 18.36–37.
The words that follow were promised at 3 Ne 18.36–37.

The power to bestow the Holy Ghost came through a two-part process. Jesus first touched and gave authorization to each of the Twelve individually (called them by name), but then they themselves had to request and receive power from the Father by mighty prayer.

notes.title: “Upon whom ye shall lay your hands”
notes.text: This is the first indication in the BoM that the laying on of hands was associated with receiving the Holy Ghost. There are two passages in the NT that mention the practice (thus do mine apostles): Acts 8.14–20; 19.1–7. Compare Moro 8.26, where the Holy Ghost comes in response to “meekness and lowliness of heart” rather than a formal ordinance.
Accounts of the Twelve bestowing the Holy Ghost occurred at 3 Ne 26.17 and 4 Ne 1.1, though neither of those mentioned laying on of hands.

notes.text: The Twelve are here referred to as elders; previously Nephite elders were only mentioned at Alma 4.7, 16; 6.1. By contrast, priests and teachers have been pervasive throughout Nephite history, beginning with Nephi ordaining his brothers (2 Ne 5.26), and then continuing when Alma1 established his church (Mos 23.17; 25.19–21).
The association of laying on of hands with ordination was seen atAlma Moroni 6.1.
This verbal formula for priesthood ordination is not currently used in the LDS Church.

notes.text: See Moroni 8.3n.

No instructions are given for the ordaining of elders. In the contemporary LDS Church, ordinances and blessings are performed by the authority of the priesthood rather than by the power of the Holy Ghost.

notes.title: “and they administered it according to the commandments of Christ”
notes.text: These sacrament prayers may have been revealed at the time of 3 Ne 18.1–14.

notes.title: “The flesh and blood of Christ”
notes.text: The ambiguity of this description with regard to the nature of the sacramental bread and wine (reflecting 3 Ne 18.7, 11, 28–29; 20.8) is resolved by the wording of the prayers that follow: the Eucharist is a memorial rather than divine substance or presence.

notes.title: “According to the commandments of Christ”
notes.text: The two sacrament prayers may have been revealed at the time of 3 Ne 18.1–14.

notes.title: “Wherefore we know”
notes.text: It is unclear who is included in the plural pronoun we.

notes.title: “Always Remember Him”
notes.text: [See the commentary on Mosiah 4:30; Helaman 5:6]

notes.title: “Bless and sanctify”
notes.text: In the Bible the two terms are only combined when God established the Sabbath at Gen 2.3; the phrase has also been used in the US Episcopal Book of Common Prayer since 1790 to consecrate the Holy Communion.

notes.title: “Sanctify”
notes.text: WB: “to make holy; to set apart or appoint to a holy, sacred or religious use.” To the souls of all those who partake of it, the reference here to souls (rather than simply “to all those who partake of it”) signals the metaphorical nature of the eucharistic consumption of the Lord’s body and blood; see 3 Ne 20.8n.

“In remembrance of the body”, 3 Ne 18.7, although that verse suggests a possible additional phrase: “in remembrance of my body, which I have shown unto you” (corresponding to “in remembrance of the blood of the Son, which was shed for them” in the prayer on the wine at Moroni 5.2). In this interpretation, the bread would represent Christ’s resurrection, while the wine represents his atonement.

notes.title: “Keep his commandments which he hath given them”
notes.text: For the Nephites, this would have referred to the teachings they had received during Jesus’s visits in 3 Ne.
“Always remember him” and “have his Spirit to be with them”, 3 Ne 18.7.

notes.title: “The Manner of Administering the Wine”
notes.text: For a discussion on the nature of Nephite wine, see commentary for 3 Nephi 18:8. See also DC 27.
The prayer over the wine is shorter than for bread in that it omits the lines about taking the name of the Son and keeping his commandments; otherwise, they are quite similar.

“In remembrance of the blood…shed for them” and “always remember him…Spirit to be with them”, 3 Ne 18.11. The two prayers are reproduced in DC 20.77, 79, with the exception of the substitution of “has given them” for “hath given them” at Moroni 4.3, a change that was made in the 1835 DC; the 1833 Book of Commandments retained the “hath.”

notes.text: The “if” clause with a negative assumes that the answer will affirm that they are indeed true (the alternative “ask if these things are true” would be more neutral); at Ether 4.11, the Lord conveys the same idea in an unambiguously positive form.

“The same today and tomorrow, and forever” is unique here, and contrasts with “the same yesterday, today, and forever,” which occurs seven times in the BoM and at Heb 13.8.

notes.text: In addition to the concluding warnings, exhortations, and invitations that Moroni extends to all of his latter-day readers in these verses, he also—somewhat remarkably—manages to weave in distinctive phrases from the last words of many of his Nephite record-keeping predecessors, as documented in the textual notes. The entire section functions something like a verbal curtain call, as we hear the voices of prophets who have appeared throughout the BoM one last time.
The phrasing here is reminiscent of Mormon’s words at Moroni 7.37–38.

notes.title: “None that doeth good among you, no not one”
notes.text: Ps 14.3 (quoted at Rom 3.12); cf. Moro 7.17.
“One among you that doeth good” may refer to JS, who translated “by the gift and power of God” (BoM title page).

notes.text: The bolded words in v. 27 are adapted from Nephi<sup>1</sup>; see 2 Ne 33.11, 13.

Both Nephi and Jacob also wrote of meeting their readers at the bar of God (2 Ne 33.11; Jacob 6.13), but only Moroni provides the question God will ask there. The idea is similar to Islamic traditions that Muhammad will meet believers in the day of resurrection and judgment, at the Pond of Abundance.

notes.text: The BoM, though written by men like Moroni, contains the words of God (a point made even more emphatically in Moroni 10:28).

notes.text: Moroni conflates the more common expressions of “speaking from the dead” (2 Ne 27.13; Morm 8.26; 9.30) and “crying from the dust” (2 Ne 3.19–20; 33.13; Morm 8.23); cf. Isa 29.4. Perhaps these are the prophecies referred to in the next verse.

notes.title: “And awake, and arise from the dust”
notes.text: Adapted from Lehi<sup>1</sup>; see 2 Ne 1.14.

The first two lines reflect Isa 52.1–2, while the next three lines echo Isa 54.2, 4 (in both cases selecting and rearranging phrases rather than quoting directly as at 3 Ne 20.36–37 and 22.2, 4). The concluding triplet reiterates language from 1 Ne 14.17; 3 Ne 16.5; 20.12; 21.4. Given the significance of the writings of Isaiah to the Nephites, it is fitting that the BoM concludes with one final example of “likening his words” to their own circumstances; see 1 Ne 19.23–24;2 Ne 11.2,8; cf.3 Ne 23.1–3.

notes.text: Moroni clarifies his exhortation in Moroni 10:30 by outlining a path to sanctification. Its emphasis on grace, sinlessness, and love has similarities with Methodist teachings about Christian perfection, but it can also be seen as an explication of Jesus’s command at 3 Ne 12.48 (Mt 5.48) to “be perfect.” The four repetitions of perfect(ed) in Christ in these verses are striking (the single other occurrence in scripture is at Col 1.28).

text.heading: Moroni 10:33
text.content: And again, if ye by the grace of God are perfect in Christ, and deny not his power, [c]1660117102[/c] [c]1660204101[/c] [c]1660207203[/c] then are ye sanctified in Christ by the grace of God, [c]1660117103[/c] [c]1660216601[/c] [c]1660204701[/c] [c]1660212101[/c] through the shedding of the blood of Christ, [c]1660205401[/c] which is in the covenant of the Father unto the remission of your sins, [c]1660011101[/c] [c]1660207202[/c] that ye become holy, without spot. [v]106[/v] [c]1660207201[/c]

notes.title: “without spot”
notes.text: Or then are ye sanctified in Christ by the grace of God—through the shedding of the blood of Christ, which is in the covenant of the Father unto the remission of your sins—that ye become holy, without spot.

While the Father’s covenants with Israel will surely be fulfilled (Moroni 10:31), this verse speaks of a new covenant by which individuals can be sanctified through Christ; cf. Ether 4.7; 1 Cor 1.2. Similarly, while words “sanctify,” “not having spot,” and “holy” at Eph 5.26–27 refer to the church, here they apply to individual believers.

narration.description: {Moroni|moroni2} bids a final farewell, and anticipates the resurrection and judgment.

text.heading: Moroni 10:34
text.content: And now I bid unto all, farewell. [c]1660104801[/c] [i]1991[/i] [c]1660302701[/c] [c]1660307201[/c] I soon go to rest in the paradise of God, [c]1660318101[/c] [i]3596[/i] [c]1660305404[/c] [c]1660313101[/c] until my spirit and body shall again reunite, [c]1660217101[/c] [c]1660304701[/c] [c]1660308201[/c] and I am brought forth triumphant [v]8[/v] [c]1660305401[/c] through the air, [i]3597[/i] [c]1660310101[/c] [c]1660304101[/c] [c]1660312101[/c] to meet you before the pleasing bar [c]1660305403[/c] of the great Jehovah, [c]1660305405[/c] [c]1660313102[/c] the Eternal Judge of both quick and dead. narration.description: {Moroni|moroni2} writes an introduction, explaining how and why the record was written and how it was managed.

text.content: Wherefore, it is an abridgment of the record of the people of Nephi, and also of the Lamanites—Written to the Lamanites, who are a remnant of the house of Israel; and also to Jew and Gentile—Written by way of commandment, and also by the spirit of prophecy and of revelation—Written and sealed up, and hid up unto the Lord, that they might not be destroyed—To come forth by the gift and power of God unto the interpretation thereof—Sealed by the hand of Moroni, and hid up unto the Lord, to come forth in due time by way of the Gentile—The interpretation thereof by the gift of God.

people.name: Moroni2
people.title: Son of Mormon2, last of Nephites

narration.description: {Moroni|moroni2} continues his introduction, explaining that he added the account of the {Jaredites|jaredites}, and emphasizes the fact that the record brings to light the divine covenant with {Israel|israel}, and implores the reader to overlook any mistakes that the record may contain, and be found spotless at the judgment day.

text.content: An abridgment taken from the Book of Ether also, which is a record of the people of Jared, who were scattered at the time the Lord confounded the language of the people, when they were building a tower to get to heaven—Which is to show unto the remnant of the House of Israel what great things the Lord hath done for their fathers; and that they may know the covenants of the Lord, that they are not cast off forever—And also to the convincing of the Jew and Gentile that JESUS is the CHRIST, [i]1137[/i] the ETERNAL God, manifesting himself unto all nations—And now, if there are faults they are the mistakes of men; wherefore, condemn not the things of God, that ye may be found spotless at the judgment–seat of Christ.
